page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the signature "A 4" printed at the foot.

p.i: stram habiturum effet justæ excusati-onis instar, dum eam in rem scriptu-rio nefcio quid subsesivis horis & subsultoriâ opera; exit tandem de re nihili, hoc est de me, & de rebus, fa-ctis, consiliis meis, jejuna hæc & (ut vereor) nimium importuna narratiun-cula.

Quam, quò mihi videmini pronio-ribus animis & auribus excepisse, eò confidentius ad illa accedo quæ super-sunt dicenda: & spero vos facile exo-ratum iri,ut quâ me attentione et pati-entiâ hastenus[?] prosecuti estis de præ-teritis rebus deserentem, eâdem prosequamini porrò, dum quid ego vobis in posterum spondeam, quidque à vobis vicissim petam, quâ potero brevi-tate exposuero. Prius illud quod at-tinet, imprimis aperte profiteor non esse

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. "hastenus" is probably "hactenus" (the ct ligature is unclear), so it is marked [?]. The underline under "Quam" is shown only as <u>. The first paragraph begins mid-sentence and so is marked cont="true". The page has no margin notes, no page number and no running head. The text ends on "esse" on the last line, which is continued text and not a catchword. Ink marks and show-through are not transcribed.
